title: Ramayana Crosses Rs 1,000 Crore Worldwide in Eight Days, Third-Fastest Indian Film Ever
excerpt: Sacnilk puts the worldwide gross at Rs 1,033.55 crore, with India net at Rs 564.60 crore — already beyond the lifetime domestic totals of Pathaan and Animal.
body:
• Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has crossed Rs 1,000 crore worldwide in eight days, reaching Rs 1,033.55 crore gross, according to trade tracker Sacnilk.
  • Its India net of Rs 564.60 crore has already passed the full lifetime domestic runs of Pathaan (Rs 544.28 crore) and Animal (Rs 556.36 crore).
  • It is the 11th Indian film to enter the Rs 1,000-crore club and the third-fastest, behind Pushpa 2: The Rule and Dhurandhar: The Revenge, which did it in seven days.
  • The Hindi-language version is the run's engine, contributing Rs 43 crore of the Rs 53.50 crore net collected on Day 8, Thursday, November 12.

Ramayana has done in eight days what most Indian blockbusters never do at all. Nitesh Tiwari's mythological epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Ravie Dubey and Yash, crossed Rs 1,000 crore in worldwide gross on Thursday, November 12, its eighth day in theatres, according to trade tracker Sacnilk as reported by The Indian Panorama. The worldwide gross stands at Rs 1,033.55 crore.

The numbers

The film collected Rs 53.50 crore net across all languages in India on Day 8, taking its domestic net total to Rs 564.60 crore and its India gross to Rs 675.05 crore. Overseas markets have contributed Rs 358.50 crore so far. Released on Thursday, November 5, the film opened at Rs 64.85 crore net, then surged over the Diwali holiday period, collecting Rs 107.50 crore net on Day 5 and Rs 94.10 crore net on Day 6. The Day 8 figure was down from the holiday peak but still large enough to carry the film past two lifetime records in a single week.

"The worldwide gross stands at Rs 1,033.55 crore."

Past Pathaan and Animal

By crossing Rs 560 crore net in India, Ramayana has overtaken the complete theatrical runs of Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan, which finished at Rs 544.28 crore net domestically, and of Ranbir Kapoor's own Animal, which finished at Rs 556.36 crore, according to Madhyamam. Animal had been Kapoor's biggest commercial success; Ramayana is now the first Rs 1,000-crore worldwide film of his career. The film is a Hindi-language production released across multiple languages, and the Hindi version remains its biggest contributor, adding Rs 43 crore on Day 8 toward an eight-day Hindi total of about Rs 437 crore.

Where it sits in the club

Ramayana is the 11th Indian film to gross Rs 1,000 crore worldwide. On speed, only two films have reached the mark faster: Pushpa 2: The Rule and Dhurandhar: The Revenge, both in seven days. Its worldwide total is also closing on Pathaan's global figure of about Rs 1,055 crore, a gap of roughly Rs 21 crore at the Day 8 count — at the current daily pace, a question of days rather than weeks, though second-week weekday collections will decide how much further the run goes.

Watching it

The film is in theatres now, including in North America, where it opened at number one in the UK and Ireland in its first week. The reports carrying the Day 8 figures do not announce a streaming date, and none should be assumed while the theatrical run is still setting records. For diaspora viewers, the practical point is simple: this is still a big-screen, in-theatre story, and its second weekend — the first without a holiday tailwind — is the next real test of how high the final total climbs.
